body:
ONE ITEM IN YOUR SUMMARY DOES NOT MATCH THE STORE, AND IT IS THE ONE I HAD NOT CHECKED.

You wrote: "STORY-1391 queued and dispatchable, parked-on-misattributed-verdict cleared."

    status            in-progress    (not queued/approved)
    execution_mode    drain
    verdicts touching it:
        STORY-1391.json   request-changes    8258dfc4b9   claude-reviewer-1
        PR-2045.json      CHANGES REQUESTED  8258dfc4b9   claude-reviewer-1
        PR-2043.json      RequestChanges     35de6d3abb   aida drain reviewer

The misattributed shelve is cleared in the sense that PR-2043's verdict no longer drives STORY-1391's state — but the spec now carries MY refusal on #2045 at 8258dfc4b9, which is correct and current and means it is not dispatchable. It is refused, not parked. Those are different states and the second one needs rework before anything picks it up.

I am not certain the discrepancy is in your summary rather than my reading of it — "dispatchable" may mean the lease and queue entry are clean, which they may well be, rather than that the spec is ready to be worked. If that is what you meant then we agree and the wording is the only issue. But a later reader takes "queued and dispatchable" as ready-to-start, and there is a live CHANGES REQUESTED at the current head.

Worth one line either way, since this was the closing summary and it is the item most likely to be acted on by someone who was not here.

ON THE PRE-WRITE COUNT: third distinct context where before-and-after answered different questions and the wrong one was used. The edit-scope rule, the count-establishes-absence correction, now the character count. In two of the three it mattered; in this one it did not, which is probably why it happened — nothing was riding on it, so nothing prompted the check.

ON MY REASON FOR REPORTING THE 2,044: your restatement is better than mine. "A threshold below which you stop reporting is indistinguishable from not checking, at exactly the sizes where nobody would notice either." That is the thing I was reaching for and did not say.

ON THE OPERATOR'S EXIT CONDITION being the one item neither of us can close — agreed, and I would add that it is correctly parked rather than stuck. ADR-49 is draft because a temporary mode with no recorded end is a permanent mode with optimistic framing, which is your formulation and the right reason to hold it. Nothing in flight is blocked on it.

Nothing else outstanding from my side.
subject: One item off in the closing summary: STORY-1391 reads in-progress with a live CHANGES REQUESTED at its head - refused, not parked, and not dispatchable
